question: Which depot a province draws on and how far it is from it: the areas, the supply groups, how a group's depot is picked, the fallback, the size a province counts as, and what the three per-province figures of the daily pass compute - for the rewrite's first piece of supply.

structs.name: CSupplyGroup
structs.comment: Areas that touch and are on one side, which share a depot. No vftable. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 3.
structs.evidence: RebuildSupplyGroups allocates 0x14 bytes for each and zeroes three words, a byte and the word at +0x10.

structs.name: COwnerAreaLink
structs.comment: One area's link to a neighbour: the area and how many edges join them. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::COwnerArea
addresses.no_signature: the object arrives in EAX and is returned in it: a constructor the compiler gave a register convention
addresses.comment: **The constructor of an area**: writes the vftable 0x15BDB50, zeroes the lists and the two flag bytes, and gives +0x94 the next number of g_owner_area_serial. 21 call sites, each after `operator new(0x98)`, which is the class's size; the one CNullOwnerArea is made by it too and has the other vftable written over. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end, 0x47C9C0..0x47CA51, bare `ret`.

addresses.name: RebuildOwnerAreas
addresses.comment: **Makes every area afresh.** ClearOwnerAreas, then for every country in the database's order and every province of its controlled list: where the province is simulated, in no area and has MaxInfrastructure above g_min_area_infrastructure, a new COwnerArea is made, flooded from it (COwnerArea::Flood) and appended to the country's list (+0xD30). When all are made, COwnerArea::BuildNeighbours on each. One caller, 0x648D48. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, bare `ret` at 0x47D15B.

addresses.name: ClearOwnerAreas
addresses.comment: Empties every country's list of areas (+0xD30) and, for every province in a real area, points the area's provinces back at the null area and frees it. RebuildOwnerAreas calls it first; ResetGameStateToStartDate's comment names the address. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, which Ghidra cuts short at each `free`; bare `ret` at 0x47D36F.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::Flood
addresses.comment: **Who is in an area.** Takes the province in - slot 1, then province->area = this - and goes through its template's edges in order, calling itself at once on every neighbour that is simulated, **has the same controller id**, is in no area and has MaxInfrastructure above g_min_area_infrastructure. The edge's kind is not looked at. Depth first, so the area's list is in the order of the walk. Ends with COwnerArea::RefreshBases. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, `ret 4` at 0x47D4DA.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::FindOpenPort
addresses.signature: int __stdcall COwnerArea::FindOpenPort(COwnerArea* area@EAX, int unused1@stack:4, int unused2@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: The id of the area's first province that has an owner, a port (+0x354), a naval base above level 0 **and a clear byte at +0x36C**, or 0. It is the 0x47E540 FINDINGS-leadership.md left unread behind `blockaded`. The two stack words are cleaned and never read. What sets +0x36C was not read, and the name is ours and inferred. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read off the listing end to end, 0x47E540..0x47E58B, two `ret 8`.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::FirstPortId
addresses.comment: The province id (+0xD0) of the first entry of the area's port list, or 0 where the list is empty. CCountry::FindSupplyDepot's last step. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C: two bare `ret`.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::RefreshBases
addresses.comment: Empties the area's port list (+0x48) and air base list (+0x58) and fills them again from its provinces: a **port** is a province with an owner, a CPort at +0x354 and a naval base whose +0x20 is above 0; an air base one whose air base's +0x20 is 1000 or more. Called after every change to the area's provinces. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, bare `ret` at 0x47E7A2.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::BuildNeighbours
addresses.comment: Empties the area's list of links (+0x34) and, for every province of the area and every edge of its template, where the province across is in a real area that is not this one, adds one to the link to that area (COwnerArea::AdjustNeighbour). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, `ret 4` at 0x47E92A.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::GetController
addresses.comment: Writes the controller's tag (+0x334, +0x338) of the area's first province through EAX, or `---` with id 0 for an area with no provinces. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C: two bare `ret`.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::AddProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 1: appends the province to the area's list unless it is there, then COwnerArea::RefreshBases and COwnerArea::RefreshDepotFlags. It does not set the province's own pointer; the callers do. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, two `ret 4`.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::RemoveProvince
addresses.comment: Slot 2: unlinks the province from the area's list, then the same two refreshes as slot 1. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, `ret 4`.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::AdjustNeighbour
addresses.signature: void __stdcall COwnerArea::AdjustNeighbour(COwnerArea* this@ECX, COwnerArea* other@EAX, int count@stack:4)
addresses.comment: Adds `count` to the link from this area to another: the 8-byte COwnerAreaLink in the list at +0x34 whose first word is the other area. A link that falls to 0 or under is unlinked and freed; one that is not there is made, at the list's end, when the count is above 0. Nothing where the two are one area. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, `ret 4` at 0x47EB41.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::RefreshDepotFlags
addresses.comment: **Writes the area's two flags.** The word at +0x68 is set to 1 - landlocked, may hold no depot - and the provinces are gone through: the first that is a port (an owner, a CPort, a naval base above 0) ends it with landlocked 0 and may_hold_depot 1; before that, a province with industry above the static at 0x1A86A14, in an area that is the area of the acting capital of the province's controller, sets may_hold_depot. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C and the listing at 0x47ECD5..0x47ED0C, two `ret 4`.

addresses.name: COwnerArea::Absorb
addresses.comment: Moves every province of one area into another - slot 1 of the receiver, then the province's own pointer - empties the giver's list, carries its links over to the receiver and takes them off the areas across, and refreshes the bases. UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince calls it where a province joins two areas of its new controller, giving the smaller to the larger. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, `ret 8` at 0x47F52E.

addresses.name: UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince
addresses.signature: void __cdecl UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince(CMapProvince* province, CCountryTag newController, CCountryTag oldController)
addresses.comment: **Keeps the areas right when a province changes hands.** Nothing where the two ids are equal and the province is in a real area. Otherwise the province leaves its area: the links its edges made are taken off, the area's slot 2 called and the province pointed at the null area; an area left empty is taken out of every list and freed, and one left with more than a province is **flooded again from scratch**, so a block cut in two becomes two areas. Then, where the new controller's id is not 0 and the province's MaxInfrastructure is above g_min_area_infrastructure, it joins a neighbouring area of the new controller - two such areas being merged, the smaller into the larger (COwnerArea::Absorb) - or a new one, and its links are made. Called from CMapProvince::TakeControl at 0x4A32C2, from 0x4A3B33 and from 0x4B808E; the caller cleans five words. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the convention from the call at 0x4A32C2, which pushes five words and adds 0x14 to ESP.

addresses.name: RebuildSupplyGroups
addresses.comment: **Groups the areas for supply.** After 0x481980 (not read), for every country in order and every real area of its list that has no supply group (+0x70 == 0): a new CSupplyGroup of 0x14 bytes, CSupplyGroup::Collect from the area, CSupplyGroup::PickDepot, and the group appended to g_supply_groups. Fifteen callers, CMapProvince::TakeControl among them. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, bare `ret` at 0x4807EC.

addresses.name: CSupplyGroup::Collect
addresses.comment: **Who shares a depot.** Sets the area's +0x70 to the group, calls slot 8 of the area's controller with it, appends the area, and goes through the area's links in order: a neighbouring area with no group is collected at once where its controller CCountry::IsSameSide with **the controller of the group's first area**, or where the neighbour is landlocked (+0x68), is not the area of its controller's acting capital, and its controller CCountry::CanOperateIn the first area's. So a puppet's land that touches its master's is one group with it, and an ally's is not unless it is a portless pocket away from the ally's capital. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C and the listing at 0x480A60..0x480B53, `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CSupplyGroup::PickDepot
addresses.comment: **Picks the group's depot.** Zeroes +0x10 and stops unless the group has more than one area or its one area's may_hold_depot is 1. Otherwise every province of every area is scored and the best kept, strictly: MaxInfrastructure, plus the province's naval base level where its area is not its owner's home, plus the same two terms for every province of its near list (+0x14C) that is in an area of this group - the naval base level being the scored province's own each time - all divided by the list's length plus one; then 2000 for the acting capital of its controller, 1000000 more where the controller is no subject, and 10000000 more where it is the first member of its faction. The id goes to +0x10 and, where it is not 0, into supply_depot_id of every province of the group. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read off the listing end to end, 0x480C00..0x480E36, `ret 4`; the decompiler drops the bodies of both inner loops.

addresses.name: RebuildAreaGroups
addresses.comment: Makes the groups COwnerArea +0x6C points at: after 0x481930 (not read), for every country in order and every area with no group, a new 0x10-byte CList, CollectAreaGroup from the area, and the list appended to g_area_groups. CMapProvince::TakeControl calls it beside RebuildSupplyGroups. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 8.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, bare `ret` at 0x47FFED.

addresses.name: CollectAreaGroup
addresses.comment: Sets the area's +0x6C to the group, calls slot 6 of the area's controller with it, appends the area, and collects at once every neighbouring area with no group whose controller is not the rebels and either CCountry::IsSameSide with the controller of the group's first area or is fighting a war beside it (CDiplomacyStatus +0x58) and is not its enemy. The supply group's rule without the limit on its second arm. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 8.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C, `ret 4` at 0x480359.

addresses.name: g_null_owner_area
addresses.comment: The one CNullOwnerArea, made on first use: a COwnerArea with CNullOwnerArea's vftable written over its own, whose slot 0 answers false. Every province in no area points at it through +0x2B4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Tested for null and filled in ClearOwnerAreas, UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince and CollectAreaFrontsForCountry, each with the same `new 0x98, construct, overwrite the vftable`.

addresses.name: g_owner_area_serial
addresses.comment: A running number: COwnerArea's constructor stores it at +0x94 and adds one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The last two instructions of the constructor before its `ret`.

addresses.name: g_supply_groups
addresses.comment: The list of every CSupplyGroup: first here, last at +4 (0x1A869B8), count at +8 (0x1A869BC). RebuildSupplyGroups appends to it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The append at the end of RebuildSupplyGroups's loop body.

addresses.name: g_area_groups
addresses.comment: The list of every group COwnerArea +0x6C points at: first here, last at +4, count at +8. RebuildAreaGroups appends to it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 8.
addresses.evidence: The append at the end of RebuildAreaGroups's loop body.

addresses.name: g_min_area_infrastructure
addresses.comment: **100: one level of infrastructure.** A province's MaxInfrastructure has to be above it for the province to be in any COwnerArea. Filled once by the initialiser at 0xCAEC50 from the float 100.5 at 0x160A684 through floorf and _ftol2_sse. Five readers, all in the area code. Three savegames bear the strict `above` out: every owned province with exactly one level carries out_of_supply_days. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The initialiser read off the listing; the comparison in RebuildOwnerAreas, COwnerArea::Flood and UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince.

addresses.name: g_depot_industry_threshold
addresses.comment: What a province's industry has to be above for its area, being its controller's home, to be allowed a depot. **One reference in the image, a read**, and nothing writes it, so it is 0. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: `cmp ecx, [0x1A86A14]` at 0x47ECE8; findRefs gives no other reference.

addresses.name: CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot
addresses.comment: **Gives a province its depot**, once a day for every simulated province (RunDailyProvincePass at 0x49EF5B) and from CInGameIdler::Enter for those still at 0. Nothing for a province with no owner or in no real area. Otherwise, with the area's supply group (+0x70): where there is one, it has two areas or more or the area's may_hold_depot (+0x69) is 1, and its depot (+0x10) is not 0, that depot; else CCountry::FindSupplyDepot asked of the controller with an empty list and no origin. Then out_of_supply_days is counted up where the depot is 0 and zeroed where it is not, and the network marked dirty. Also called from 0x4A3546, 0x4B8279 and, on the farthest province when its distance exceeded 500, 0x682D3B. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C again with the group read.
addresses.revises: `inferred` becomes `confirmed`, and the comment's unidentified `area+0x70` with its `+8` and `+0x10` is the area's CSupplyGroup, its count of areas and its depot; `area+0x69` is may_hold_depot. The source moves to the network's write-up.

addresses.name: CCountry::FindSupplyDepot
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CCountry::FindSupplyDepot(CCountry* this, CProvince* province, void* visited, CCountry* origin)
addresses.comment: **The depot of a province whose group gave it none.** 0 where the province's area is in `visited`, has no owner or is no real area; else the area is added and `origin` taken to be `this` where null. Then, only where the province's controller is `this`, in order: (a) where the area may hold no depot, each neighbouring area of a country origin CCountry::IsFriendly with, asked by recursion with that country as origin; (b) where origin is a subject, each neighbouring area of its overlord's; (c) origin's acting capital where the area is that capital's area; (d) where origin is `this` and the area has a port, the province with the most MaxInfrastructure in and around it inside the area; (e) each neighbouring area held by origin, by a puppet of origin or by a puppet of origin's overlord; (f) each held by a friend. The first answer above 0 is returned. Last, where origin is `this`, the area's first port (COwnerArea::FirstPortId), else 0. `ret 0xC`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C with every callee identified, and the listing for the calls and the tail at 0x4F2F47.
addresses.revises: `inferred` becomes `confirmed`. The comment gave only the capital's case and 'recurses through the area's list and +0xF34/+0xF38'; it is the fallback behind the supply group, and the order of its steps and what each asks is now read. The source moves to the network's write-up.

addresses.name: SupplyCapacity
addresses.comment: **How much a province can pass on in a day**, thousandths, through `out`. 99999000 where the province's `capital` byte (+0x2B0) is set - the controller's capital and every province that touches it. Otherwise the effective infrastructure (modifier 12 times 1000 plus modifiers 13 and 14, held between 10 and 1000) is turned into a level, 10000 x infra / 1000; the level is squared over 1000, or 1000 where it is under 1000; times INFRA_THROUGHPUT_IMPACT; times OWNED_AND_CONTROLLED_THROUGHPUT_CAP_BONUS where the owner is the controller; times 1000 plus the controller's SUPPLY_THROUGHPUT modifier plus its technology's supply_throughput (+0x10). Only reads. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the two constants are the floats 10.5 at 0x160A680 and 10000.5 at 0x160A648 through floorf.
addresses.revises: The comment said only 'unlimited where the province byte +0x2B0 is set'; the formula is now written out, and that byte is the capital or a province beside it. The source moves to the network's write-up.

addresses.name: SupplyLoss
addresses.comment: **What a load loses crossing a province**, thousandths, through `out`. SUPPLY_TAX, halved where the owner is the controller; times 1000 plus the mud term - muddyness (+0x84) x MUDDYNESSSUPPLYTAXMODIFIER / 1000 where the province is not frozen (+0x88 == 0) - plus, where the controller CCountry::IsEnemy of the owner, PARTISAN_EFFECT_ON_SUPPLY_TAX x the province's LOCAL_PARTISAN_SUPPORT modifier (id 0x4C) x (1000 - suppression held between 0 and 1000) / 1000; then the controller's technology supply_transfer_cost (+0xC) is added and the result floored at 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; the modifier is read at [province+0x114]+0x260, which is id 0x4C.
addresses.revises: The comment built the partisan term 'from the province's +0x84 when +0x88 is zero': those two are the mud. The partisan term is the modifier with id 0x4C, less what suppression takes off, and only on ground held by an enemy of its owner. The source moves to the network's write-up.

addresses.name: SupplyNeed
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SupplyNeed(CMapProvince* province@stack:4, int* suppliesOut@stack:8, int* fuelOut@EDI)
addresses.comment: **What the units in a province ask for in a day**, supplies through the stack pointer and fuel through EDI, both zeroed first: CUnit::SupplyConsumption and CUnit::FuelConsumption summed over the **land units** standing there (+0x2B8, the virtual at +0x3C) whose owner is the controller or is not at war with it, neither being the rebels - the owner is not looked at before a game is under way; over **the wings based there**, the list at +4 of the province's air base object (+0x54); and over **the fleets in port there**, the list at +4 of its naval base object (+0x58). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read from the decompiled C; +0x54 and +0x58 are the record's home_base_ptr and naval_base_station.
addresses.revises: The comment called +0x54 and +0x58 'two further unit lists whose meaning is not established'; the struct already names them. The source moves to the network's write-up.

struct_fields.name: neighbour_areas_first
struct_fields.comment: The list of the areas this one touches. **Each node's payload is a pointer to an 8-byte COwnerAreaLink** - the other area and how many edges join the two - made and counted by COwnerArea::AdjustNeighbour. Walked in order by CSupplyGroup::Collect and CCountry::FindSupplyDepot, so the order the links were made in is the order areas are tried in. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
struct_fields.evidence: COwnerArea::AdjustNeighbour allocates 8 bytes, stores the area at +0 and the count at +4, and hangs it in a 0x10-byte node.
struct_fields.revises: The type was CList<COwnerArea*>: the payload is a pointer to a pair, not to the area. Every reader takes one more step through it, which is why the decompiler showed the area's fields as `vftable[3]` of the payload.

struct_fields.name: air_bases_first
struct_fields.comment: The area's provinces with an air base of level 1 or more; count at +0x60. Filled by COwnerArea::RefreshBases beside the port list. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: landlocked
struct_fields.comment: No province of the area has a working port. Written by COwnerArea::RefreshDepotFlags. CSupplyGroup::Collect takes a landlocked area into a group of a country its controller may operate in; RunDailyProvincePass reads it on the first day a province is out of supply. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
struct_fields.evidence: Written as the low byte of a word at 0x47EC23 and 0x47ED0C.

struct_fields.name: may_hold_depot
struct_fields.comment: **The area may hold a depot of its own**: it has a working port, or it is the area of its controller's acting capital and has industry. Written by COwnerArea::RefreshDepotFlags; read by CSupplyGroup::PickDepot, CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot and CCountry::FindSupplyDepot. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0x47ECF0 and as the high byte of the word at 0x47ED0C.

struct_fields.name: supply_group
struct_fields.comment: **The supply group the area is in**, set by CSupplyGroup::Collect. Its +0x10 is the depot every province of the group draws on. FINDINGS-supply.md had it as 'the area-level override that gets first refusal on a province's label'. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 3.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored at 0x4809E2; read in CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot and compared in CSupplyGroup::PickDepot at 0x480D0F.

struct_fields.name: serial
struct_fields.comment: A running number given by the constructor from g_owner_area_serial. No reader was looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.

struct_fields.name: areas
struct_fields.comment: The areas of the group, the one it was started from first; count at +0x8. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 3.
struct_fields.evidence: CSupplyGroup::Collect appends to it; CSupplyGroup::PickDepot walks it.

struct_fields.name: depot
struct_fields.comment: The province id of the group's depot, or 0 for a group that was given none. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4.

struct_fields.name: edges
struct_fields.comment: How many edges join the two areas; the link goes when it reaches 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 2.
struct_fields.evidence: Added to and tested by COwnerArea::AdjustNeighbour.

struct_fields.name: size_class
struct_fields.comment: **How big the province counts as, 1 to 4**: set by CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry at 0x49183E..0x491860 from bbox_width + bbox_height - under 30 pixels 1, under 60 2, under 90 3, else 4. CSupply::SpreadFromDepot multiplies it by 1, 2 or 3 for the province's infrastructure to get the step it adds to supply_depot_distance, and CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure uses it as its step. Not a distance: an edge carries its own at +0xC. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 6.
struct_fields.evidence: Read off the listing of CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry; the constructor zeroes it at 0x4A94AF and no other store in the map code is to a template's +0x24.
struct_fields.revises: Was `unknown_24`, 'a per-province traversal cost' whose value 'was not sampled, so whether it is normally 1 is open'. It is 1 to 4 by the bounding box.

struct_fields.name: simulated
struct_fields.comment: **The province takes part in this session.** MarkSimulatedProvinces sets it on every province in a campaign and, in a scenario, only on the scenario's own list - the two stores at 0x68600F and 0x686062 are the only ones in the image. Supply, the areas, the daily province pass and the Simplified Terrain loop all skip a province with it clear. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 1.
struct_fields.evidence: dispscan over the whole of .text for a store to +0x13D: two, both in MarkSimulatedProvinces.
struct_fields.revises: Was `unknown_flag_13d`, 'still unidentified', while the record's own entry for MarkSimulatedProvinces already said what it is.

struct_fields.name: near_provinces_begin
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector of **every province within two edges**, each once, in the order met - and so the province itself, once it has a neighbour; sea provinces too. Filled by the province's reset at 0x496480 from its template's edges and each neighbour's. CSupplyGroup::PickDepot scores a province over it and SuppressionNearProvince sums over it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4.
struct_fields.evidence: Read in the decompiled C of 0x496480, lines of the two nested loops, and at 0x480CCD..0x480CEA.

struct_fields.name: near_provinces_end
struct_fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x14C; +0x154 is its end of storage. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4.

struct_fields.name: near_provinces_begin
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector of **every province within two edges**, each once, in the order met - and so the province itself, once it has a neighbour; sea provinces too. Filled by the province's reset at 0x496480 from its template's edges and each neighbour's. CSupplyGroup::PickDepot scores a province over it and SuppressionNearProvince sums over it.
